title: Rast wins Hockenheim Race 1 for a fifth straight victory
dek: René Rast won DTM Race 1 at Hockenheim for Audi from third on the grid, 0.354 seconds clear of Robin Frijns, while Gary Paffett took the points lead after a late safety car.

chapters.title: A title fight and a farewell
text: The DTM came to Hockenheim for the last two races of 2018 with the championship still open and Mercedes about to leave the series after 30 years. Paul di Resta, in the #3 Remus Mercedes, led the standings on 229 points, four ahead of his team-mate Gary Paffett, with René Rast, the 2017 champion, a further 30 back on 199 for Audi. Mercedes had already secured the manufacturers’ and teams’ titles, so the drivers’ crown would complete a clean sweep in its final season.

Rast was the only one of the three who had nothing to lose, and he arrived in the form of his career. He had won four races in a row across the Nürburgring and Red Bull Ring weekends and called himself the outsider, though he insisted that anything can happen in a finale. Audi’s motorsport chief Dieter Gass summed up the plan for the weekend as going all in.

The track had been kind to the title contenders before. Paffett won the season-opener here in May, and the same weekend produced a long duel between him and BMW’s Timo Glock. Glock warned that the opposition had grown much stronger since then and that matching those results would be hard, while Paffett spoke of mixed feelings about a last weekend for the team he had driven for over 15 years.

chapters.title: Auer takes pole, Paffett closes in on di Resta
text: Lucas Auer put the #22 Silberpfeil Mercedes on pole with a 1m32.635s, 0.102s faster than Paffett, who had led the session with a 1m32.737s until the final minute. Glock was third for BMW on 1m32.751s, ahead of Rast on 1m32.847s and Augusto Farfus’s BMW on 1m32.880s. The qualifying points, three for pole and two for second, cut di Resta’s lead over Paffett to just two.

The order on the grid was reshuffled by penalties. Glock and Philipp Eng, both of whom had collected a third warning at the Red Bull Ring, each had to drop five places. That left Glock eighth and Eng 12th, and moved Rast up to third, di Resta, who had qualified eighth, to sixth and Robin Frijns to seventh. Nico Müller was fifth, Edoardo Mortara ninth and Joel Eriksson tenth, with Loïc Duval only 16th.

Marco Wittmann, the 2018 Norisring winner for BMW, had a very different Saturday. He hit the wall at the Sachs-Kurve late in the morning practice session, and his RMG crew could not repair the #11 car in time to run in qualifying. He started from the back of the grid in 18th.

chapters.title: Paffett leads, Rast fights back
text: Auer made the best start, but Paffett took the lead from his team-mate on the first lap in the Mercedes Arena. Rast was slow away and lost a place to Farfus, which looked costly with a championship slipping away.

He took the place back on lap four and passed Auer a lap later, using DRS to close up. Auer was by then losing speed and eventually rolled into the pits with a mechanical problem, ending his race on the sixth lap. Up front, Paffett and Rast pulled away from the rest of the field, with Paffett about two seconds in hand.
Di Resta’s afternoon went the wrong way. He ran fifth early on, but contact with Frijns pushed him back to seventh.

chapters.title: Back and forth at the hairpin
text: Rast was the first of the leaders to make the compulsory tyre stop, and Paffett covered it a lap later. That gave Rast the better tyres on the road, and he caught Paffett on the Mercedes driver’s first lap out of the pits. He ran wide at the hairpin on his first attempt to pass, but made it stick at the Mercedes Arena the next time round.

Paffett would not let him go. He kept the pressure on and the two spent several laps swapping DRS blasts and looking for a gap, until on lap 23 Paffett regained the lead. Rast answered within moments, going down the inside at the hairpin to take the position back at the Spitzkehre. The sequence recalled the long fight Paffett had had with Glock at the opening race of the year.

chapters.title: A door on the back straight
text: The fight was neutralised on lap 26 when the driver’s door came off Farfus’s BMW on the back straight and the safety car was called. Seven laps remained at the restart. Rast got the better getaway and slipped clear, while Paffett was immediately under pressure from Glock.

Wittmann, who had worked his way towards the top ten from the back of the grid, went off at the restart and finished seven laps down. For Mercedes it was the point at which the afternoon turned. Team principal Ulrich Fritz said the pace had been good until the safety car, but that everyone else was quicker afterwards.

chapters.title: Frijns charges, Paffett slips to fourth
text: The restart favoured those on fresher tyres, and Frijns had stopped late. He picked off Paffett and then Glock, taking second on the penultimate lap, and he crossed the line only 0.354s behind Rast. Glock was third, 1.856s down, after climbing from eighth on the grid; Paffett finished fourth, 2.641s behind the winner.

Duval was fifth after moving up from 16th, ahead of his Phoenix team-mate Mike Rockenfeller and Müller. Di Resta, who had looked set for a good finish, lost out to the three charging Audis in the closing laps and came home eighth, with Bruno Spengler and Mortara completing the top ten.

Following both races at the Nürburgring and both at the Red Bull Ring, it was Rast’s fifth win in a row. He said he had not expected to add another that afternoon. The result also reshaped the title fight. Paffett went back to the top on 239 points, six ahead of di Resta and 15 clear of Rast, leaving three drivers in contention for the final race on Sunday.

facts.v: Rast’s Race 1 victory was his fifth consecutive win, the first time any driver had won five DTM races in succession.
